rows.evidence: Q1: Materials and Methods <U+2013> field experiment in 2019/20 at Werer Agricultural Research Center, split-plot RCBD with drip and furrow as main plots and four irrigation levels as sub-plots, three blocks. Q2: Results, 'Effects of irrigation system and irrigation level on water use efficiency' and Table 3 <U+2013> drip at 100% ETc yielded 16666.6 kg/ha versus 7078.2 kg/ha for conventional furrow at 100% ETc; text states drip at 100% ETc increased maize yield by 57.53% compared with conventional furrow (farmers' practice). Q9: Table 3 reports LSD (1680.4) and CV (12.19%) for yield; Table 2 reports LSD and CV for the main-effect yield comparison.
rows.notes: Single site, single season, single crop (maize), plot-scale (4.5 m x 6 m plots). Yield measured by one method (plot harvest), no second independent method. No intermediate variable (e.g. soil water status, evaporation) reported as a result; soil moisture formulas are given in methods but no soil-water results are presented. The authors state drip at 100% ETc is suited to resource-rich investors because of high variable cost, but this is a condition for economic attractiveness rather than for the yield effect, so Q7 is no. No limitations of the study are stated. Q9 is borderline: dispersion is given as CV and LSD rather than SD/SE per treatment.

rows.evidence: Q1: Materials and Methods <U+2013> own field experiment (2019/20, Werer, split-plot RCBD, three blocks). Q2: Results section on water use efficiency <U+2013> drip at 100% ETc saved 33.7% of irrigation water compared with conventional furrow (farmers' practice); Abstract <U+2013> highest seasonal water requirement 701.7 mm under conventional furrow at 100% ETc; Table 3 <U+2013> WUE 2.15 kg/m3 for drip 100% ETc versus 0.60 kg/m3 for conventional furrow.
rows.notes: Water saving is reported as a single percentage derived from applied irrigation depths; no dispersion (SD, SE, CI, range) is reported for applied water or water saving (CV/LSD are given only for yield/WUE). Single method, single site/season/crop, plot scale. No intermediate variable such as application efficiency, runoff, deep percolation or soil evaporation is measured and reported. No conditions stated as requirements for the water saving; no limitations stated.

rows.evidence: Q1: Materials and Methods <U+2013> own field experiment (2019/20, Werer, split-plot RCBD with drip vs furrow main plots, four ETc levels, three blocks). Q2: Results section and Table 3 <U+2013> drip at 100% ETc yielded 16666.6 kg/ha versus 4753.1 kg/ha for alternate furrow at 100% ETc; text states 71.5% maize yield increase compared with alternate furrow irrigation (with 24.58% more irrigation water used than alternate furrow). Q9: Table 3 reports LSD (1680.4) and CV (12.19%) for yield.
rows.notes: The passage's '24.58% loss of irrigation water' corresponds to the study's statement that drip at 100% ETc used 24.58% more water than alternate furrow; this row is rated on the yield (crop_production) effect only. Single site, season, crop and plot scale; one measurement method; no mechanism variable reported; no required conditions or limitations stated. Q9 borderline (CV and LSD rather than per-treatment SD/SE).

notes: Full text appears complete. One-season (2019/20) split-plot field trial at a single research station in semi-arid Ethiopia on maize; results reported as treatment means with letter groupings, LSD and CV, plus a partial-budget economic analysis. The study provides no explicit limitations section.
